indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B1.5.1.2: Appreciate the natural and human features of the local environment and the need for keeping the environment clean
indicator.objective: know that clean air and water are essential to human health

skills.description: Explain why clean air is important
Explain why clean water is important
Identify what happens if air or water is dirty
Identify simple actions to keep air and water clean

misconceptions: Smoke is just air, so it is safe.
Dirty water is safe to drink if you cannot see the dirt.
Water from any source is safe to drink.

questions.stem: Why do we need clean air?
options: To breathe well and stay healthy
hints: Clean air is good for you.
questions.explanation: We need clean air to breathe well and stay healthy.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not realize the importance of clean air.

questions.stem: Why do we need clean water?
options: To drink safely and stay healthy
To wash our hands in dirty water
questions.explanation: We need clean water to drink safely and stay healthy.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think any water is safe.

questions.stem: What happens if you drink dirty water?
questions.explanation: Drinking dirty water can make you sick because it contains germs.
questions.misconception: Pupils may drink from unsafe sources.

questions.stem: What happens if you breathe in a lot of smoke?
options: You can cough and get sick
questions.explanation: Breathing in smoke can make you cough and get sick.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think smoke is harmless.

questions.stem: Which of these helps to keep the air clean?
questions.explanation: Planting trees helps keep the air clean because they absorb some gases and release oxygen.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think burning rubbish cleans the air.

questions.stem: Where can we find clean air?
options: In a park with many trees
Near a busy road with many cars
questions.explanation: Clean air is found in places with many trees and less smoke, like a park.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think all outdoor air is clean.

questions.stem: Which of these is a source of clean water?
options: A river with rubbish in it
hints: It is not open to rubbish.
questions.explanation: A covered well is more likely to contain clean water.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think all water sources are clean.

questions.stem: What should you do with rubbish to keep the environment clean?
hints: Do not throw it in water.
questions.explanation: Throwing rubbish in a bin helps keep the environment clean.

questions.stem: Ama sees a stream with rubbish in it. Is the water clean?
options: No, but it is safe to drink
questions.explanation: The water is dirty because of the rubbish.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think visible water is safe.

questions.stem: Which activity makes the air dirty?
questions.explanation: Burning rubbish produces smoke that makes the air dirty.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think sweeping makes air dirty.

questions.stem: Name one thing that makes the air dirty.
questions.explanation: Smoke, dust, and fumes from cars make the air dirty.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not recognize common air pollutants.

questions.stem: Name one thing that makes water dirty.
questions.explanation: Rubbish, dirt, and waste make water dirty.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think water is always clean.

questions.stem: Why is it important to keep our water sources clean?
options: So we can drink safe water and stay healthy
questions.explanation: It is important to keep water sources clean so we can drink safe water and stay healthy.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not connect clean water to health.

questions.stem: A community wants to keep their air clean. What should they do?
options: Plant more trees and reduce burning
questions.explanation: Planting more trees and reducing burning helps keep the air clean.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not know how to improve air quality.

questions.stem: Kofi has a choice between water from a tap and water from a muddy puddle. Which should he choose and why?
options: Tap water, because it is clean
Muddy puddle, because it is natural
Muddy puddle, because it is cold
Tap water, because it is colourful
questions.explanation: Kofi should choose tap water because it is clean and safe to drink.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think natural water is always safe.

questions.stem: What can happen to a person who breathes in dust every day?
questions.explanation: Breathing in dust every day can cause breathing problems.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think dust is harmless.

questions.stem: Why is it dangerous to throw rubbish into a river?
options: It pollutes the water and makes it unsafe for drinking and animals
It makes the river flow faster
questions.explanation: Throwing rubbish into a river pollutes the water, making it unsafe for drinking and for the animals that live in it.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not understand the wider impact of water pollution.

questions.stem: Write two ways you can help keep your environment clean.

criteria.description: Names one correct action (e.g., throwing rubbish in a bin, planting trees, not burning rubbish)

hints: What do you do with your rubbish?
questions.explanation: You can help by throwing rubbish in a bin and planting trees, among other actions.

questions.stem: Explain why clean air is important for your health.

criteria.description: States that we need air to breathe
States that dirty air/smoke makes us sick or causes coughing

hints: We breathe air all the time.
questions.explanation: Clean air is important because we breathe it, and dirty air can make us sick.

questions.stem: Tell your teacher why you should not drink water from a dirty puddle.

criteria.description: States that the water is dirty
States that it has germs and can make you sick

questions.explanation: You should not drink from a dirty puddle because it contains germs that can make you sick.
